Adani Ports taps more global lenders for $2.9-billion Evos acquisition funding
sum: First Abu Dhabi Bank and DBS are among the lenders being approached, even as MUFG has committed up to €2.8 billion as sole underwriter for the European liquid-storage acquisition.

Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone is looking to bring UAE’s First Abu Dhabi Bank and Singapore’s DBS Bank into the financing of its proposed acquisition of European liquid-storage operator Evos, widening the lender group beyond Japan’s MUFG, which has underwritten the transaction, people aware of the development told Moneycontrol.The company is discussing a mix of debt and its own equity contribution for the acquisition, which values Evos at €2.6 billion, or about $2.9 billion. Borrowings could account for half or more of the funding, with the eventual mix depending on how much cash Adani Ports chooses to deploy, the sources said. The discussions would broaden participation in a transaction for which financing commitments are already in place. MUFG is the sole underwriter and has committed up to €2.8 billion, Adani Ports said in its November 5 announcement. The equity contribution under consideration would allow Adani Ports to use its cash generation alongside bank funding. The company reported a cash balance of Rs 12,502 crore as of September 30. Indian public-sector banks have also been considered, although their participation appears less likely under the plan being discussed, the sources said. Evos operates liquid-storage terminals in Europe, earning fees for storing, handling and blending fuels and chemicals for energy companies, industrial customers and commodity traders. Emails sent to Adani group and DBS did not elicit a response till the time of publication. “As a matter of policy, FAB does not comment on individual client relationships, transactions, or market speculation. We remain committed to supporting our clients across the markets in which we operate and conducting our business in accordance with the highest standards of governance and regulatory compliance," a spokesperson for First Abu Dhabi bank said in an email response. Adani Ports has agreed to acquire 100 percent of Netherlands-headquartered Evos from Igneo Infrastructure Partners. The transaction has an equity value of €1.18 billion and an enterprise value of €2.56-billion, which includes Evos’ debt.

Mitsubishi Electric stock: Mega-constellation study begins
sum: Mitsubishi Electric has entered a new space-infrastructure study with four Japanese partners, expanding its strategic focus on satellite systems beyond its established defense and space activities. The company announced the memorandum of understanding on Monday, Nov. 9, after the partners signed it on Friday, Nov. 6. The announcement came in a Mitsubishi Electric release.

Mitsubishi Electric, NTT, NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS, MUFG Bank and Development Bank of Japan will examine the technical and business feasibility of a mega-constellation. The concept describes a coordinated network of numerous satellites designed to provide services across broad areas of the Earth.

The study covers satellite communications, Earth observation, satellite-based positioning, navigation and timing, as well as space data centers. The partners also plan to examine communications during disasters and in areas with limited connectivity, together with more efficient use of satellite information.

The memorandum starts a joint examination rather than a commercial rollout. The companies will identify technical requirements and challenges and work toward a concrete cooperation framework. The release does not announce a launch schedule or a completed investment decision, leaving the eventual commercial scope dependent on the studies.

Mitsubishi Electric will conduct technical studies on the overall system design and integration. Its work will consider how satellites, ground stations, communications networks and operating systems can be combined based on user needs. The company said the aim is to develop a system concept that supports efficient construction and operation and allows future expansion.

The company will also examine applying its Digital Space Interface to the initiative. Mitsubishi Electric describes the interface as an open common interface for satellite information processing. It is intended to make the addition and updating of large software packages on satellites in orbit more flexible, potentially supporting changes to services after deployment.
For investors, the immediate significance is strategic rather than a reported earnings contribution.

sum: The Rs 667.53-crore IPO comprised a fresh issue of 45.45 lakh shares aggregating to Rs 150 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 1.57 crore shares worth Rs 517.53 crore. While the company will receive the proceeds from the fresh issue, the OFS component will allow existing shareholders to partially offload their holdings.

The company had fixed the IPO price band at Rs 313-330 per share, with a lot size of 45 shares. Retail investors applying for one lot at the upper end of the price band were required to make a minimum investment of Rs 14,850.

The public issue, which opened for subscription on October 27 and closed on October 29, 2026, received an overall subscription of 9.47 times. The qualified institutional buyers (QIB) portion was subscribed 18.81 times, while the non-institutional investors (NII) category saw 12.81 times subscription. The retail portion was subscribed 2.71 times.
IIFL Capital Services, JM Financial and Nuvama Wealth Management were the book-running lead managers to the issue, while MUFG Intime India acted as the registrar.

SFC Environmental Technologies Ltd. proposes to utilise the net proceeds from the issue to prepay all or part of certain outstanding borrowings of Rs 42.23 crore availed by the company and its wholly owned subsidiary, Vasudha Waste Treatment Pvt. Ltd. It will allocate Rs 74.92 crore towards funding working capital requirements, with the remaining proceeds earmarked for general corporate purposes.

SFC Environmental Technologies Ltd.’s total income increased 13% to Rs 821 crore in FY26 from Rs 727 crore in FY25. Profit after tax (PAT) rose 5% to Rs 160 crore from Rs 152 crore during the same period.

Incorporated in March 2005, SFC Environmental Technologies Ltd. is an environmental technology company providing solutions for wastewater treatment, recycling and reuse, and solid waste treatment. Its wastewater business is primarily based on proprietary C-Tech technology, an advanced sequencing batch reactor process. As of July 31, 2026, the company had commissioned 728 wastewater treatment installations, with its technologies facilitating the treatment of 17,511.11 million litres of wastewater per day. It also offers recycling solutions using ultrafiltration, reverse osmosis and membrane bioreactor technologies.

sum: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc (MUFG) moved down by 3.10%. The Banking & Investment Services sector is down by 2.05%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: JPMorgan Chase & Co (JPM) down 1.39%; Goldman Sachs Group Inc (GS) down 2.90%; Bank of America Corp (BAC) down 1.37%.

Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group experienced downward pressure during the trading session, driven primarily by shifting expectations surrounding Japanese monetary policy and broader financial sector profit-taking. Public remarks from Bank of Japan officials signaled a cautious approach toward further interest rate adjustments, dampening market expectations for immediate follow-up rate hikes. Because domestic mega-banks rely on rising interest rates to expand net interest margins and boost interest income, any indication of a measured policy trajectory directly tempers immediate earnings acceleration expectations for major Japanese lenders.

In addition to domestic monetary policy dynamics, global macroeconomic headwinds and bond yield fluctuations weighed on institutional sentiment. Global financial equities faced profit-taking following a period of strong year-to-date performance across the sector. Philippines – Strait of Hormuz closure: Impact of higher oil prices and more
sum: - We see the Philippines Peso as vulnerable and USD/PHP possibly rising above the 60 levels if the Iran and Middle East conflict is sustained and the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, with oil prices already reaching above US$100/bbl at the time of writing: While we do not yet know how the Iran and Middle East conflict will play out from here, it’s important to stress our current base case USD/PHP forecast of 58.00 by 4Q2026 assumes a resolution after March 2026 and implicitly for oil prices to fall towards the US$70/bbl levels. Our model-based estimates tell us that USD/PHP could range between 59.00-60.00 in a scenario of US$90/bbl oil prices, and between 60.00-61.00 with US$100/bbl oil prices, especially if this is coupled with a hawkish Fed. Of course, not all things are equal in practice, and the BSP may choose to not just pause on policy rates but even hike rates, which would provide some offsetting support to PHP. Overall, we see our scenario and sensitivity analysis as reasonable given the meaningfully different nature of today’s crisis.

- This time is different in this crisis - it is not just about higher oil prices but a potential looming energy shortage, with the Philippines and Asia disproportionately hit by a prolonged Strait of Hormuz closure: We highlight three key areas of direct energy supply shortage stress in this crisis - crude oil, petroleum products, and natural gas and natural gas liquids like LPG/propane.

- First, crude oil. 95% of the crude oil that the Philippines imports and on average 65% that Asia imports comes from the Middle East, with relatively limited ability to bypass the Strait of Hormuz chokepoint even with existing pipelines out of Saudi Arabia and the UAE.

- Second, refined petroleum products especially in Asia are facing significant risk of shortages especially in jet fuel, diesel and gasoline, with production shut-ins in the Middle East exacerbated by reduction in refinery runs in Asia and some initial signs of export restrictions on refined petroleum products from our region. While the Philippines only imports 3% of its refined product needs directly from the Middle East, shortages from regional refineries and the global spillovers of higher product prices will no doubt impact the Philippines.

EGM today: The contentious non-compete fee and secondment clauses in MUFG–Shriram Finance deal
sum: January 14 is a critical day for Shriram Finance, as its shareholders convene for an extra-ordinary general meeting to seek approval for a multi-billion dollar investment by Japan’s MUFG in the company.

Two out of three leading proxy advisory firms — Institutional Shareholders Services Inc and Ingovern — seem ready to welcome the equity that will flow into India’s leading retail non-banking financial company (NBFC). But former Sebi executive director JN Gupta’s firm Shareholders Empowerment Services (SES) has flagged some concerns questioning the core of the transaction and whether it was structured just to avoid an open offer.

The critical issue are the sanctity of handing out a $200 million non-compete fees to Shriram group’s promoter entity Shriram Ownership Trust (SOT) and the preferential rights sought by MUFG, which potentially masks its investment as strategic and not just a financial investment.

That said, as is with many deals in the past, it’s possible that shareholders may ratify the transaction. Yet, the questions raised call for attention, particularly from the regulators to ensure that an out-of-rule-book deal doesn’t set precedent for more to come.

Non-compete fee is usually an additional compensation extended to the seller or exiting shareholder(s) to ring fence the incoming investor. In simple words, it’s akin to a parting gift paid to ensure that the selling or exiting shareholder doesn’t engage or restart the same line of business which could be to the detriment to new shareholders and promoters.
Extending a non-compete fee is a common practice globally. It acknowledges the exiting investor’s role and contribution to the company.
But in India, especially with listed companies, such an arrangement is seen as threading in the grey.

Shriram-MUFG deal may test rules on non-compete fee for promoters
sum: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) Bank has agreed to pay the fee to the promoter of Shriram Finance (SFL) as part of a broader investment plan under which the Japanese lender will acquire a 20% stake in the Chennai-based shadow bank for $4.4 billion.

The payment—amounting to nearly 5% of the deal value—is intended to prevent Shriram Ownership Trust (SOT), the promoter entity, from launching a rival lending, credit, or fintech business under the Shriram brand or any other name.

Non-compete fees are not uncommon in M&A transactions but are typically paid to promoters who exit a business after selling their stake and relinquishing control, thereby protecting the buyer’s interests.
When Holcim acquired Gujarat Ambuja Cement (GACL) in 2006, for instance, the Swiss major paid a non-compete fee to promoters Narotam Sekhsaria and Suresh Neotia after they sold out and ceded control.
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi), requires that all shareholders receive “equitable treatment” and that promoters not be paid extra amounts “by whatever name it may be called”.

Regulation 26(6) of Sebi’s listing rules states that a promoter cannot enter into any agreement with shareholders or third parties to receive compensation or profit-sharing from transactions in the company’s securities, unless the board and public shareholders approve it. Rules also mandate that if a non-compete fee is paid to a promoter, it must be factored into the open offer price for public shareholders.
Unlike the GACL deal, which involved a sale of shares and a change in control—thereby triggering an open offer—SOT is not selling any shares to MUFG, and there is no change in control at SFL.

items.t: MUFG’s next CEO Hanzawa seeks growth to close gap with global rivals
sum: Widely seen as a safe choice, whether he can further elevate the group with 400 trillion yen in assets will be closely watched

[TOKYO] Junichi Hanzawa, the next chief executive officer of Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG), will take the reins of Japan’s largest bank as it rakes in record profits. His challenge will be sustaining that growth beyond the windfall of rising interest rates.

Hanzawa, 60, who is currently head of the main banking unit, will succeed Hironori Kamezawa on Apr 1, MUFG said in a statement on Tuesday (Dec 16). Kamezawa, 64, who has been CEO since 2020, will become chairman.

Long considered the heir apparent, Hanzawa is typical of a traditional bank leader in Japan: a lifelong insider who built his career as a corporate staffer, playing a key role in strategic planning and regulatory affairs. While widely seen as a safe choice, whether he can further elevate the group with 400 trillion yen (S$3.3 trillion) in assets will be closely watched.

“Not only in Japan, where the business environment is improving due to rising rates, we want to close the gap with global financial institutions,” Hanzawa said at a briefing. “For that, having a growth strategy in Asia and the US is important.”

In the reshuffle, Masakazu Osawa, senior managing corporate executive, will succeed Hanzawa as chief of lending arm MUFG Bank. Hiroyuki Seki, head of global markets business, will become president of brokerage unit Mitsubishi UFJ Securities Holdings.
Like its rivals, MUFG is projecting profit will reach new heights, last month raising its net income forecast to 2.1 trillion yen for the fiscal year ending Mar 31.

items.t: How Japanese banking giant MUFG is using AI
sum: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) is going all out to use artificial intelligence (AI) in all parts of its business, moving beyond using AI as a tool to deploying AI agents that will work alongside its employees.

In doing so, the Japanese banking giant aims to become an AI-native company. This vision was laid out by Morito Emi, head of MUFG’s digital strategy division, at the MUFG Fintech Festival in Singapore, where he spoke about the progress of the bank’s AI efforts.

Even though MUFG has deployed AI tools for all employees, only half regularly use them, he said. To address the gap and prepare for the future, MUFG is not only doubling down on efforts to spur greater AI adoption internally, but also paving the way for agentic AI.

“We are entering an era of AI agents, one where AI shifts from being just a tool to taking on actual roles as digital employees working alongside humans,” said Emi. “What will matter most is how we make use of our unique data.”

To realise its vision, MUFG is focused on three main priorities: company-wide AI training, creating an architecture for AI agents to operate effectively and safely, and enhancing its data strategy, where it is rebuilding its business model to make its data more accessible to AI agents.

In July 2025, MUFG started the Hello AI @ MUFG campaign to promote the use of AI as a core part of its corporate culture. Over 6,000 employees took part in the first event of the campaign, a prompt challenge where staff compete to write the most effective instructions for generative AI.

A key part of MUFG’s efforts to build up its AI capabilities is working with top AI technology suppliers. In October 2024, it teamed up with OpenAI to give its employees access to ChatGPT Enterprise. OpenAI will also help with developing advanced AI use cases and provide dedicated support.
